about: SkewD's published measurements; the release summary's SkewD and SkewD-MV entries are built from it
build: Andrey at commit 4c1cda49b of the functional-models line, from before 0.18.0. The SkewD code of 0.18.0 and 0.19.0 is the same, except that each column's mean and variance are summed over its sorted values (so they do not depend on the row order), which changes the standardized values in their last digits: refits of 3 of these pairs, both criteria, and one 6-variable graph at small budgets gave the same edges on both builds, with likelihoods that agree to about 1e-9 relative, and PC's class as SkewD-MV computes it, with the same column order, is the same on all 80 graph datasets under both builds. The criteria are read from one fit per pair

comparators.SkewD authors' recorded outputs: SkewD-LL as recorded per dataset by the code published with the paper (commit 312632b), run by the authors with the paper's arguments on the same data files; checked by a reduced fresh run (reference_check in the lane file)

verdict_rule: per set (pairs, seeds 0-19, each criterion) or per graph size (seeds 0-19, then 20-39 fresh): D = error(Andrey) - error(the authors' recorded output) per dataset; worse when the 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of mean D lies entirely above 0, better when entirely below, a tie otherwise; 10,000 resamples, default_rng(0). Floors: for pairs the Wilson 95% lower bound of the share right above 0.5 (coin_flip_floor; the column order is swapped on exactly 10 of each 20 pairs, so the majority direction is right on half), for graphs the empty graph (floor). A graph fit over 4 h of CPU counts as failed and scores the worst DAG's SHD; none was
seeds_note: pairs: seeds 0-19, pairs 1-10 of each of a pooled set's two files or pairs 1-20 of a single file; graphs: seeds 0-19 are datasets 1-20 and the fresh seeds 20-39 datasets 21-40 of the authors' files
fit_protocol: each fit in a job of its set on one core with one BLAS thread, one timed fit at the defaults; pairs killed at 2 h and graphs at 4 h of CPU, which no fit reached; times are CPU seconds

regimes.skewd_pairs: the SkewD paper's skewed pairs, 1,000 rows: additive (ANs) and location-scale (LSs) noise models at three noise skewnesses (-0.455, 0.985 and 1.750), and Tagasovska et al.'s (2020) Gaussian-noise location-scale sets LS and LS-s, 20 pairs each, the column order swapped on 10
regimes.skewd_mv_graphs: the SkewD paper's skew-normal location-scale graphs (Table 2): Erdos-Renyi DAGs with as many edges as variables, 6 and 10 variables, 1,000 rows, sources uniform on [-3.5, 3.5], 20 datasets per size and 20 fresh

data_identity: each recorded pair output stores the standardized data it fitted; it agrees to 1e-12 with the standardized (cause, effect) Andrey's arm read on 320 of the 320 pairs of the eight sets, seeds 0-39

recorded_outputs.about: the recorded outputs over every pair of each set and the first 100 graphs of each size: the share each criterion names right, the paper's Table 5, and the mean SHD (a reversal counting 2), the paper's Table 2

oracle_class.about: the likelihood stage on the true class, scored as the graph
the likelihood stage on the true class, scored as the graph

reference_check.about: the code published with the paper (commit 312632b, NumPy 1.26.4, cmaes 0.13.1, scikit-optimize 0.10.2), run fresh on a subset of the datasets and compared with the authors' recorded outputs for the same datasets. The rule was proposed with the 11 earlier fresh pairs (9 independence agreements) and the 2 graphs whose PC class is fully directed already known, before any of the 4 new pairs or the 3 graphs whose class leaves edges to orient finished, and accepted by the maintainers with 1 of those pairs and 2 of those graphs known: at least 2 of the 4 new pairs and 2 of the 3 graphs finish; the likelihood direction agrees on every fresh pair; the independence direction on all but one in five; each fresh graph within 2 SHD of its recorded graph. The authors' optimizers are stochastic, so their scores differ from the recorded ones; on graphs whose PC class is fully directed only PC is checked

frontier.about: beside other Andrey methods on the same datasets, in the same jobs: a comparator dominates when its paired error interval lies below SkewD's (share right for pairs, SHD for graphs) and its median CPU seconds are lower

not_measured: SID is not reported. The paper's IGCI, ROCHE, QCCD, HOST and GraN-DAG baselines have no Andrey implementation and were not run. The fresh run of the authors' code covered the graphs whose classes are cheapest to score
